title: Field on the axis of a charged ring
caption: For a ring of charge Q = 10 nC and radius a = 0.1 m, E_z = kQz/(z² + a²)^{3/2}. At z = 0.1 m this is 3.2 kN C⁻¹ (the lesson's 3.2 × 10³). It is zero at the centre by symmetry, peaks at z = a/√2 = 0.071 m with 3.46 kN C⁻¹, and for z ≫ a falls as 1/z², like a point charge.
alt: Graph of the axial field against distance z: zero at the ring's centre, a peak of 3.46 kilonewtons per coulomb at z = 0.071 m, then a slow fall.
description: The horizontal axis is the distance z along the axis from the ring's centre in metres; the vertical axis is E in kN C⁻¹.
At z = 0 the contributions of opposite sides cancel: E = 0.
The field peaks at z = a/√2 = 0.071 m with 3.46 kN C⁻¹.
At z = 0.1 m: E = 3.2 kN C⁻¹ ≈ 3.2 × 10³ N C⁻¹.
Far away it falls as kQ/z².
